concept.name: Rate of change
concept.definition: A pure momentum oscillator measuring the percentage change between the current close and the close n periods ago, plotted as an unbounded line around zero; the StockCharts ROC page notes the indicator is also referred to simply as Momentum.
concept.intuition: It is rise over run for prices: positive while the price is higher than n periods ago, negative while lower, with distance from zero showing how fast the move is.
concept.mechanics: Compute (Close - Close n periods ago) / (Close n periods ago) x 100, default n = 12. Used for zero-line trend bias, security-specific overbought/oversold extremes (often +/-10%), and divergences.
concept.formula: ROC(n) = ((C_t - C_{t-n}) / C_{t-n}) x 100, where C_t is the current close.
concept.failure_modes: Zero-line crosses whipsaw in ranges, and divergences fail often because strong trends frequently start with the sharpest ROC spike, printing a bearish divergence mid-advance.
concept.misconceptions: A falling ROC is not a falling price - price still rises as long as ROC is positive; it only means the advance is decelerating.
concept.example: Close today 55, close 12 days ago 50: ROC = (55-50)/50 x 100 = +10%.
